Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Mara made the booking through TideBoard on Tuesday evening and received confirmation number BK-4186. The room is on the second floor, beyond the green stairwell, and the building’s side entrance is the easiest route for carrying in the band’s equipment.

The rehearsal is for the group’s first full run-through of a set they plan to play at the Lantern Room on November 2. The band members are Mara, who plays drums; Eli Navarro, on bass; and June Park, on guitar and vocals. They are not using the rehearsal to finalize the concert set list. Their immediate aim is to check transitions, agree on tempos, and find out whether the new closing song works at the same volume as the rest of the set. Mara has asked the others to bring their current charts, but she has not asked anyone to prepare a new arrangement.

Mara chose the east room because it has a drum kit available and enough floor space for the group’s two amplifiers. The kit includes a five-piece maple set, a pair of crash cymbals, a ride, a hi-hat, a kick pedal, and a drum throne. The house does not supply snare wires or sticks, so Mara will bring her own snare, sticks, and brushes. She will also bring a small tool roll, a spare clutch, and a folded rug to put beneath the kick drum. The room has a basic microphone and two vocal stands, although the band expects to use only one microphone during this rehearsal.

1. Before leaving home, Mara will check that the snare case contains the drum key, brushes, and both pairs of sticks. She will put the charts in a waterproof folder rather than leaving them loose in the car. Eli is bringing a bass, a small amplifier, and a power strip. June is bringing her guitar, pedalboard, and instrument cable. The band has agreed that each person is responsible for taking home their own equipment, while shared items can stay in the room until the booking ends.
2. At 9:45, Mara will meet Eli at the side entrance and collect the room key from the front desk. June expects to arrive separately, but she has the booking number and knows which room to use. The front desk has asked visitors not to block the delivery bay, even for a short unload. If the side entrance is locked when Mara arrives, she will use the intercom by the main entrance and ask the desk attendant to open it; she should not leave the cases unattended outside.
3. The first twenty minutes are set aside for unloading, tuning, and setting the kit height. After that, the band will play the opening three songs without stopping unless there is a safety problem or a cable has come loose. They will pause to make notes after the first run-through, then repeat the two transitions that felt uncertain. The final half hour is reserved for the closing song and a quiet pack-down, not for extending the booking.

Mara has marked two possible tempo ranges in her notebook because the group has not settled on a speed for “Window Light.” The slower version keeps the bass line relaxed, while the faster version makes the chorus feel more urgent. She will ask Eli and June to try both tempos before they decide which one serves the song better. Nothing in the booking note says that the band has chosen a final tempo, and Mara does not want the rehearsal notes to make it sound settled before everyone has played both versions.

The booking confirmation says that the east room may be used for amplified rehearsal, but the building’s quiet-hours rule still applies in the hallway and common areas. Mara has told the band to keep their instruments in cases while moving through the building and to avoid testing amplifiers outside the room. The room’s posted maximum is six people, so the three musicians may have a guest sit in, but they have not invited anyone. If a guest is added, Mara will update the front desk before the rehearsal rather than assuming the extra person can enter without being recorded.

When Mara called the rehearsal house to ask about parking, attendant Luis said, “The two short spaces beside the side door are for unloading, not for leaving a car through the session.” Mara will park in the public lot on Alder Street after the instruments are inside. The lot charges by the hour, and the rehearsal house does not validate parking. Eli has offered to move his car after unloading as well, so the band does not need to reserve either short space for the full booking.

The group will keep a written record of any changes they make to the arrangements. Mara will note the tempo they try, the order of the transitions, and whether the kick drum needs more or less damping. June will mark guitar cues on her chart, and Eli will write down any bass changes that affect the endings. They are using one shared notebook, but each musician can photograph the relevant pages before leaving. The notes are for this rehearsal only; they are not a replacement for the charts or a promise that every suggested change will be used at the concert.

At 1:10, Mara will stop the final run-through even if the band has not played the closing song again. That leaves time to return the house cymbals to their cases, clear the floor, and check the corners for sticks or cables. The session is complete only when the kit is back in its original arrangement and the room key has been returned to the front desk. If the band finishes early, they may pack quietly and leave before 1:30, but they should not keep playing once the room is cleared.
